title: Symbol-wise interloping in secret-key typical authentication
summary: Determine whether allowing an adversary to interlope one channel symbol at a time changes the typical authenticated-capacity region of a secret-key DM-AIC.

formal_statement.body: For every discrete memoryless adversarial interlope channel in the source model, compare two adversaries: one that either replaces the decoder's entire length-$n$ observation or leaves it unchanged, and one that may replace symbols individually. Prove that the closures of their achievable message-rate, typical-authentication-rate, and key-consumption-rate triples are equal, or exhibit a DM-AIC for which the two regions differ.

scope.domain: Secret-key information-theoretic authentication over discrete memoryless adversarial interlope channels
assumptions: The encoder and decoder share the source model's secret key
The adversary observes the source-defined noisy channel output before choosing an interlope action
Authentication is measured by the source's typical-authentication criterion
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected forward citation proves region equality for every source-defined DM-AIC or gives a channel separating block-wise and symbol-wise interloping.

citations.label: Graves--Perazzone--Yu--Blum, Secret Key-Enabled Authenticated-Capacity Region, Part II

progress.summary: Remark 1 states that symbol-by-symbol adversarial operation is likely immaterial to the authenticated-capacity region but remains an open question.
